title: C9063 — Tweeter LH A-pillar
introduction:
I read an audio connector by keeping each positive circuit paired with its matching negative description. Mixing speaker descriptions is like swapping name tags at band practice: the labels still look tidy, but the connections tell the wrong story. Here, the drawing's shaded middle cavity corresponds to the unused row, while the populated positions have repeated circuit entries.

Use the identity table, harness drawing and cavity map together, followed by the pigtail catalog. The tweeter title and the woofer and left-middle function descriptions have an unexplained relationship; equipment applicability remains unresolved. The summary pin count also conflicts with the drawing and pigtail cavity count. This page teaches reference reading, with physical viewing direction, Size and gauge conventions, access, testing and replacement outside its established scope.

That makes the catalog relationship traceable, but it cannot resolve the component-description ambiguity or establish a replacement choice. No splice or terminal-service method is taught here.

originalAuthorHold: The identity table gives Pin Count 5, but the drawing labels cavities 1–3 and the pigtail table gives Cavities 3. Repeated assignment rows do not establish additional physical cavities; the summary count needs review.

The title identifies TWEETER LH A-PILLAR, while populated function rows describe SPEAKER LEFT FRONT DOOR (WOOFER) and SPEAKER LEFT MIDDLE. Their relationship and equipment applicability are unexplained. Retain these descriptions pending focused review; do not silently rename the component or select a circuit set.
